distractors.reason: 'Hardly' means almost not at all, so 'work hardly' says the opposite of the intended meaning of diligent effort.
'Badly' means poorly or incorrectly. We say 'work hard' for effort, not 'work badly' for quality of effort.
'Strongly' is not used with 'work' to describe effort. Native speakers say 'work hard'.

example_sentence: They work ___ to finish the project on time.
l1_interference: Türkçe konuşanlar zarfı fiilden önce koyma eğiliminde olabilir ve 'hard work' gibi bir yapıyı fiille karıştırabilir. İngilizcede zarf genellikle fiilden sonra gelir: 'work hard'.
explanation: In English, adverbs of manner and degree usually follow the verb they modify. 'Hard' describes the amount of effort, and this pattern is fixed in the phrase 'work hard'.

related_collocations.example: She studied hard for the exam.
I did not sleep well last night.
Please listen carefully to the instructions.

memory_tip: HARD = with great effort | HARDLY = almost not at all | The adverb comes AFTER the verb: work hard, sleep well
